_comment: infra/seccomp/chromeless.json — seccomp profile for the chromeless container (T57). DENY-list profile: defaults to ALLOW (Chromium has a wide syscall surface and ALLOW-listing it is brittle), then explicitly blocks the syscalls Chromium has no business calling. Lifted from Docker's default deny set; pruned to syscalls that are NEVER needed by chromium-as-renderer + supervisord + python http.server + gorilla websocket Go services. When tightening further, do it incrementally and watch the audit log on /proc/<pid>/seccomp_filter for SCMP_ACT_LOG hits.
_chromium_note: Chromium has its own seccomp-bpf inside each renderer when --no-sandbox is NOT set. We pass --no-sandbox today (v1 expedient — see Dockerfile), so this OS-level seccomp is the only seccomp layer between the renderer and the host kernel. Until T44's gVisor/Kata decision lands, this is the line of defense.

syscalls._rationale: Module load/unload — kernel-rooting paths. No userland use case.
Direct hardware / firmware access. Container should never touch this.
Mount / namespace manipulation. Container is already namespaced; renegotiating namespaces is a sandbox-escape primitive.
Time / domain-name modification. Affects the whole container.
Reboot / power management. Pod lifecycle is K8s's job, not the container's.
Kernel keyring. Has been CVE-prone (CVE-2016-0728, CVE-2017-2671). Chromium does not use it.
BPF program load. Powerful kernel-side execution; Chromium does not use it. eBPF is also a CVE class.
userfaultfd has been a kernel-exploit primitive (CVE-2021-22555 etc.). Chromium has no use for it.
Swap. Container should never manage swap.
Quotas, accounting. Not a userland concern.
Memory-policy manipulation across NUMA. Powerful, container-scoped abuse vector.
Personality, perf_event_open: have been used in chains against the kernel; renderer doesn't need them with --no-sandbox.

ptrace lets one process inspect/modify another. Chromium-with-sandbox uses it; --no-sandbox doesn't. shareProcessNamespace makes ptrace particularly dangerous (one container could ptrace another). Block.
process_vm_readv/writev let one process read/write another's memory directly. Same threat model as ptrace.
kcmp leaks pid-and-resource information across processes — useful for kernel-info-leak chains.
